text: Because the shot-noise photon cost grows as 4 to the power B (quadrupling per bit), analog optics is cheap at ___ precision and punishingly expensive at high precision, which is why photonic machine-learning accelerators converge on 4-to-8-bit inference workloads.
explanation: Analog optics is cheap at low precision and punishingly expensive (about 4 times per bit) at high precision, so photonic accelerators deliberately target 4-to-8-bit inference, the regime where the optical energy-per-operation advantage survives; ask for 16 or 32 bits and the shot-noise floor forecloses the advantage.
